title: Six Thousand Years Offshore
question: How did people go from diving for food to reaching the deepest trench?
hook: People were diving into the sea around 4500 BC, yet a craft only dove 10,915 meters into the Mariana Trench in 1960.
idea: Ocean exploration moved forward together with better ships, diving, navigation, depth measurement and maps.

beats.prompt: Put these ocean milestones in order, from earliest to latest.
items: Pytheas sails north out of the Mediterranean
Magellan's ships sail around the world
The Trieste dives into the Mariana Trench
beats.explain: Egyptian sailing vessels date to about 4000 BC, Pytheas to 325 BC, Magellan's voyage to 1519–1522 and the Trieste dive to 1960.

beats.prompt: Match each explorer to what they contributed.
pairs: Using the North Star to find latitude
Using a marine chronometer for longitude
A map of the Mediterranean region
A voyage to study compass variation
beats.explain: Each one pushed forward navigation or mapping, the skills ocean exploration grew alongside.

beats.prompt: Between 1405 and 1433, China sent seven costly voyages to spread its influence and impress neighboring states. What happened to these voyages?

choices.label: They grew into a permanent yearly fleet
choices.feedback: Tempting, since the voyages were a show of power, but they did not become a lasting program.

choices.label: They were ended after a short time
They went on to sail around the world
choices.feedback: Sailing around the world is credited to Magellan's ships, in 1519–1522.

beats.explain: The voyages were expensive, and they were stopped after a short time.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Charles Darwin sailed on the Beagle from 1831 to 1836.
On the way he explored the Galapagos and many other areas.
That work led him to the ideas of natural selection and evolution.
So the Beagle made the first scientific ocean voyage.
beats.explain: Edmund Halley's voyage of 1698–1700, to study the variation of the magnetic compass, was probably the first mainly scientific voyage, long before the Beagle.
